quotes.text: Every decision encoded in those bicep templates is actually a decision about who gets to decide things. Who can create a resource? Who approves policy changes? How fast can a team get what they need?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes landing zone code as an expression of organizational decision rights.

quotes.text: Gatekeeper governance designed to reduce risk actually increases it. Because the more friction you create in the official path, the more teams find unofficial paths.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the central paradox of the episode in two sentences.

quotes.text: You are still making the same governance decisions you were before. But now you are making them once in your code and executing them every time without fail.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why automated subscription vending keeps governance intact while removing wait time.

quotes.text: Version pinning discipline means never referencing latest or main. Never, those are moving targets. You reference 1.3.2, a specific version.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: A concrete, actionable rule for consuming Bicep modules safely.

quotes.text: When you see a team using an external data warehouse you ask them what problem it solves. Is it about the speed? Is it a specific feature? Is it the cost?
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Turns shadow IT from something to block into a source of requirements.

takeaways: Landing zone code encodes organizational decision rights, and gatekeeper governance that slows provisioning pushes teams into shadow IT.
Subscription vending, versioned Bicep modules consumed by pinned version, and audit-first policy rollout make the governed path faster than the ungoverned one.
Treat the landing zone as a versioned platform product: centralize what must be uniform, distribute what must move fast, and measure provisioning time, compliance trends and drift.
hook: Your Azure landing zone may be slowing teams down so much that they build around it. This episode is for cloud architects and platform teams running Azure at scale, and shows how Bicep modules, subscription vending and guardrail-style governance turn the official path into the fastest path.
